terra.problem: The text says she uttered a curse about the silver, not that she put a curse on whoever took it.
“You’d think so” endorses the idea that Micah should be shamed. Papa Dorin does not shame people.
“Just” and “in one breath” add a timing the text does not give between the curse and the blessing.
Saying the silver is not headed to the tabernacle settles what happens to all of it. The text accounts for two hundred shekels used for the image and idol, not the destination of the rest.
The explanation repeats three times that the image and idol are in Micah’s house, without adding personality or insight.
“With the family” places Micah’s family in the house with the image and idol, which the text does not say.
The passage does not say that the shrine, ephod and household idols are all in Micah’s house.
The explanation simply repeats that the priest was a son rather than a brother. It has no distinct Papa Dorin voice.
“Nobody called him over” goes beyond the text. It does not say whether anyone called for him.
“It’s not a huge deal” assesses the value of the offer without support from the passage.
Saying a son “fits” Micah’s request for a father figure overlooks the reversal: Micah asked the Levite to be his father, but the Levite became like a son to Micah.
